definitions.explanation: A person who works aboard a ship, especially one engaged in manual labor on deck rather than in a commanding or navigating role. The word has a somewhat traditional or literary flavor.

examples.japanese: {水夫|すいふ}たち⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{帆|ほ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{張|は}った→張る：12583_haru⟧。
⟦{祖父|そふ}→祖父：01452_sofu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{若|わか}い{頃|ころ}、{水夫|すいふ}⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{世界|せかい}→世界：01447_sekai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{回|まわ}った→回る：01150_mawaru⟧。
examples.english: My grandfather traveled around the world as a sailor when he was young.

examples.japanese: ⟦{古|ふる}い→古い：00488_furui⟧⟦{小説|しょうせつ}→小説：01434_shousetsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{嵐|あらし}→嵐：01695_arashi⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{闘|たたか}う→闘う：17304_tatakau⟧{水夫|すいふ}たち⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{姿|すがた}→姿：03363_sugata⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦{描|えが}かれている→描く：02013_egaku⟧。
examples.english: Old novels often depict sailors battling storms.

notes:
A compound of {水|すい} (water) and {夫|ふ} (man, laborer). Also read as かこ in classical Japanese. The word evokes traditional seafaring and appears frequently in literature, historical accounts, and stories about the age of sail. In modern maritime usage, ⟦{船員|せんいん}→船員：22495_senin⟧ or ⟦{乗組員|のりくみいん}→乗組員：21154_norikumiin⟧ are the standard terms for crew members.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {水夫|すいふ}⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{働|はたら}く→働く：00503_hataraku⟧: to work as a sailor
- {水夫|すいふ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{雇|やと}う→雇う：02320_yatou⟧: to hire sailors
- {水夫|すいふ}⟦{長|ちょう}→〜長：04665_chou⟧: boatswain, chief deckhand

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{船員|せんいん}→船員：22495_senin⟧: crew member, seafarer — the modern, official term for anyone working aboard a ship
- ⟦{乗組員|のりくみいん}→乗組員：21154_norikumiin⟧: crew member — used for the crew of ships, aircraft, or spacecraft
- {船|ふな}{乗|の}り: sailor, mariner — a slightly more colloquial word with a romantic or adventurous connotation
- {海員|かいいん}: seaman, maritime worker — a formal term used in labor law and maritime regulations
